classification.difficultyReason: Select the nonnegative-speed branch and evaluate the supplied model at two speeds before subtracting the stopping distances.

content.prompt:
Nadia is investigating stopping distances for a car travelling at different speeds.
To model this she uses the equation $d = 0.01s^{2} + 0.7s$, where $d$ is the stopping distance in metres and $s$ is the speed of the car in km/h. The graph of this equation is drawn on the left.

spec.description: Supplied upward-opening parabola with both branches, arrowheads, square grid, labelled axes and curve equation. Source teal is represented by house blue.
spec.mathematics: d=0.01s^2+0.7s; axes s=-70 to 70 and d=-50 to 90; grid interval 10; horizontal labels -60,-40,-20,0,20,40,60; vertical labels -40,-20,20,40,60,80; vertex (-35,-12.25).
spec.answerVisibility: The whole supplied curve remains visible for the student to highlight; the applicable domain is not highlighted.

children.label: a
children.prompt:
Nadia knows that only part of this curve applies to her model for stopping distances.
Highlight the part of this curve that applies for stopping distances.

answer.worked: Highlight the curve from the origin to the right, including the origin. Speed cannot be negative, so the model applies for $s\geq 0$.

spec.description: Complete supplied graph with its nonnegative-speed branch highlighted in red and the origin included.
spec.mathematics: The applicable domain is s>=0. The red branch begins at (0,0) and continues for positive speeds.

children.label: b
children.prompt: What is the difference between the stopping distances in a school zone when travelling at a speed of 40 km/h and when travelling at a speed of 60 km/h?
